purpose: Tramadol is used to treat moderate to moderately severe pain, such as pain after surgery, injury, or from chronic conditions like arthritis. It can be used for short-term or long-term pain depending on what your doctor decides is best for you. It is a prescription-only medication.
how_it_works: Tramadol works in two ways to help reduce pain. First, it attaches to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord called opioid receptors, which helps block pain signals. Second, it also increases the levels of certain natural chemicals in your brain called serotonin and norepinephrine, which also help reduce how much pain you feel.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, dizziness, headache, drowsiness, and dry mouth are the most common side effects. Some people also feel lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly. Taking it with food can help reduce nausea.
warnings: Tramadol can be habit-forming, so take it exactly as prescribed and do not share it with others. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as it can cause serious breathing problems. It can also cause seizures, especially at higher doses or if you have a history of seizures. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially antidepressants, as dangerous interactions can occur.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain, but your doctor will decide the right dose for you. The maximum dose is generally 400 mg per day. Extended-release tablets are taken once daily for around-the-clock pain. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions exactly.
